messages:
sasha: Nightly perf alerts flagged a regression on fp8 serving for long-context chat workload. throughput down ~18% on average, and p99 token latency up from ~72ms -> ~120ms. noticed many fallbacks to generic int8 kernel.
kevin: Ugh. Is this the multi-shape batching path again? We recently changed the kernel cache key generation.
maria: I pulled a profile. The continuous-batcher is creating batches with mixed seq-len shapes, then kernel selector rejects fp8 fast-path because kv-cache alignment bits don't match. fallback occurs due to `kernel_key != cached_key`.
sasha: exact. profiler snippet (flame trimmed):
```
serving/runtime/kernel_select  42%  <-- fast-path rejected early
serving/runtime/generic_kernel  38% <-- fallback exec
serving/batcher/shape_fold    12%
kvcache/read_alignment      8%
```
now the surprising part: the kvcache alignment mismatch is caused by incremental KV splits when sequence padding triggers a soft-slab allocator re-chunk.
we lose FP8 kernels because the runtime requires exact stride/packed-shape match to use quantized kernels; even though data could be reinterpreted to match.
now the model's calibration also contributed: a small fraction (~0.4%) of calibration runs produced outlier scales that changed the quant-flag for some layers, causing some kernels to be marked "mixed-precision-incompatible".
we have two failure vectors: 1) shape/stride mismatch at kernel lookup; 2) quant-compatability flip from calibration outliers.
math: measured per-token throughput drop 18% -> estimated cost +14% per 1k tokens.
logs:
```
[2026-06-12T03:44:11Z] kernel_selector: miss reason=kv_stride_mismatch expected=32 actual=24
[2026-06-12T03:44:11Z] quant_checker: layer_attention: fp8_ok=false scale_outliers=5/1200
```
questions: can we make kernel selection more tolerant? or normalize KV strides at batch time?
kevin: options: - normalize batch layout: re-pack KV buffers to common stride before kernel lookup (expensive copy, but rare) - introduce a tolerant key that allows reinterpret of stride when padding only (no data movement) - bin batches by (seq_len, kv_stride) in the continuous-batcher (best-fit bin packing) to avoid mixing shapes - per-request micro-batching when continuous-batcher detects >10% shape variance
owen: I'd lean toward binning in the batcher + a small fast-path that can reinterpret contiguous memory if stride mismatch only due to trailing padding. re-packing should be last resort.
maria: For the calibration flips: we should tighten outlier handling in calibration pipeline. currently we set per-tensor scale by median+2sigma for activations; a few traces with large activations push the scale. proposal: - record percentile ratio (99.9/99) and if >X, treat as outlier and clamp scale to model-level default - add a per-layer quant-stability flag that prevents runtime toggles between fp8/int8 across minor cal runs
kevin: Also: kernel metadata needs to include a "shape_mask" that indicates padding-only mismatches can be ignored. runtime can do a cheap check: if stride mismatch but padding coverage >= 95% then allow reinterpret.
sasha: prototype config I used to reproduce:
```
# small hack in continuous-batcher
if mixed_shapes and max_len/min_len <= 1.25:
  allow_mixed=true
  batch_key = (model, quant_profile, kv_stride_masked)
```
it repros perf locally on my devbox.
infra-bot: nightly-deck: build/7491 ran kernel-selection A/B with binning=enabled; traffic sample=10k requests.
infra-bot: results: median token latency -3.2%, p99 -7.8% for enabled vs baseline (non-repacking). CPU overhead +1.1%.
sasha: good signal. next steps: - (kevin) implement shape_mask tolerant key (runtime) — safe >=95% padding coverage. owner: kevin. ETA 2d. - (maria) adjust calibration pipeline to add outlier clamp + stability flag. owner: maria. ETA 3d. - (owen) change continuous-batcher to bin by kv_stride and seq_len quantiles, fallback to micro-batch. owner: owen. ETA 4d. - (sasha) add unit perf test that simulates KV slab re-chunking with mixed seq lens + calibration jitter. owner: sasha. ETA 2d.
kevin: i'll push a small change to kernel_key serializer to include a `shape_mask` boolean and a confidence metric. will add telemetry for "tolerant-lookup-hit" vs "exact-hit".
maria: once we have the telemetry we can tune threshold from 95 -> 99 if we see any quality delta. also will add an eval that checks logits shift for FP8 tolerant-lookup.
owen: note: we must be careful with memory aliasing when reinterpreting strides. add assert in debug builds to validate repeated runs produce identical outputs for a given random seed.
sasha: agreed. i'll file a short RFC and link to this thread.
kevin: ack. thanks for the reproduction steps — saved me a full day.
maria: nice! :shipit:
infra-bot: created perf-issue #2137 and linked nightly-deck 7491.
